- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use 3-period moving average.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or declining, model often fails to capture downward momentum; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model tends to drift toward historical mean; apply mean reversion with 3-day smoothing.  
- When sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for each day sentiment remains above 0.67.
